title: Tokens and context windows

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Tokens and context windows

children.text: Models read tokens, not characters, and they can only see a fixed window of them. Both your bill and your failures come back to this.
What this lesson covers
Understand tokenisation and why cost is per token
Budget a prompt against the context window
Recognise the failure modes of an overflowing context
This lesson sits in LLM Fundamentals, part of Building AI Apps with LLMs. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Understand tokenisation and why cost is per token
Budget a prompt against the context window
Recognise the failure modes of an overflowing context
proTip: Count tokens before you ship a prompt template. Long system prompts are billed on every single call.

title: Temperature and sampling

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Temperature and sampling

children.text: Sampling parameters decide how the next token is picked. Low temperature for extraction and classification, higher for anything that should feel varied.
What this lesson covers
Trade determinism against variety with temperature
Know what top-p changes and when to touch it
Pick settings per task rather than globally
This lesson sits in LLM Fundamentals, part of Building AI Apps with LLMs. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Trade determinism against variety with temperature
Know what top-p changes and when to touch it
Pick settings per task rather than globally

title: Choosing a model for the job

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Choosing a model for the job

children.text: The largest model is rarely the right default. Match capability, latency, and price to what the specific step of your product needs.
What this lesson covers
Weigh capability against latency and cost
Route easy steps to a smaller, faster model
Build an evaluation before committing to a choice

keyPoints: Weigh capability against latency and cost
Route easy steps to a smaller, faster model
Build an evaluation before committing to a choice

title: Designing the system prompt

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Designing the system prompt

children.text: The system prompt sets role, constraints, and refusals. It is followed more reliably than instructions buried in user content, so the load-bearing rules belong here.
What this lesson covers
Separate durable rules from per-request input
State constraints and refusals explicitly
Keep it short enough to stay affordable per call
This lesson sits in Prompting That Holds Up, part of Building AI Apps with LLMs. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Separate durable rules from per-request input
State constraints and refusals explicitly
Keep it short enough to stay affordable per call

title: Structured output and JSON

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Structured output and JSON

children.text: If your code consumes the output, it needs a schema. Constrain the shape, then validate the response before anything downstream touches it.
What this lesson covers
Constrain responses to a declared schema
Validate the parsed output at runtime
Handle the case where the model returns nothing usable
This lesson sits in Prompting That Holds Up, part of Building AI Apps with LLMs. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Constrain responses to a declared schema
Validate the parsed output at runtime
Handle the case where the model returns nothing usable
proTip: Validate structured output even when the API guarantees a schema. A retry is cheaper than corrupt data.

title: Tool calling fundamentals

title: Building an agent loop

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Building an agent loop

children.text: An agent is a loop: call the model, run the tool it asked for, feed the result back, repeat. Every loop needs a stopping condition it cannot argue with.
What this lesson covers
Structure the call, execute, feed back cycle
Bound the loop with iteration and token limits
Log each step so failures can be replayed
This lesson sits in Tool Calling and Agents, part of Building AI Apps with LLMs. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Structure the call, execute, feed back cycle
Bound the loop with iteration and token limits
Log each step so failures can be replayed

title: Guardrails and evaluation

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Guardrails and evaluation

children.text: Without an evaluation set you cannot tell an improvement from a regression. Guardrails then enforce the limits your evaluation exposed.
What this lesson covers
Build a small, honest evaluation set early
Score changes against it before shipping
Enforce boundaries the model must not cross
This lesson sits in Tool Calling and Agents, part of Building AI Apps with LLMs. It assumes what came before it and leads directly into the next lesson in the module.

keyPoints: Build a small, honest evaluation set early
Score changes against it before shipping
Enforce boundaries the model must not cross
proTip: Thirty real examples you curated beat a thousand you generated with the same model you are testing.

title: Streaming responses to the browser

thumbnail.alt: Video thumbnail for Streaming responses to the browser
